expected.summary: Layout runs with no board open: it opens the board {doc}, answering its known open prompts; the board is found open afterwards.
Layout has this board open already: nothing to open; exit 0.
A Layout session opens .pcb files; refused before Layout is asked.
No board file at that path.
A Designer and a Layout are both running, and the call names the file to open but no --session: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.
A forward-annotation job on this board has ended, and no job get or job list has read its end yet, so its operation still locks part of the board: E_CONFLICT target_locked.
Run under a scope file that does not cover the target (the board); nothing is previewed to the application's files or sent.
While a forward-annotation or pcb export job of this tool runs in Layout: E_BUSY; nothing is opened.
A person leaves a modal dialog open in Layout: the session is blocked; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with the dialog's title.
Layout goes away after OpenDocument was sent.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Layout cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

expected.summary: Layout has this board open with unsaved changes of this tool: nothing is opened, exit 0; the adapter then reports the board clean although Layout still holds the changes.

rows.reason: The read-back is whether the board is open; Layout's open itself checks that the board is open afterwards and fails with E_NATIVE_FAILURE otherwise, so there is no stored value that can differ.
